title: fix(sql): validate forward foreign keys at DDL admission
body:
## What type of PR is this?

- [ ] API-change
- [x] BUG
- [x] Improvement
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Test and CI
- [ ] Code Refactoring

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #29852

## What this PR does / why we need it:

A parent CREATE could apply its planned incoming FK to a replacement child that no longer declared it. Stale negative dependencies could also leave a newly available parent or child unbound. CREATE admits its declared name domain, checks the actual binding/commit watermark, and uses the existing applied-logtail/replan owner before effects. Incoming repair binds current catalog declarations against actual child definitions, preserves complete unrelated constraints, and updates each child once. Planner and executor share FK decoding and validation.

Lifecycle transitions retain the existing admission, SQL token and deferred rollback owners. Retained transitions use FastFail; DROP INDEX waits for its provisional physical definition before acquiring names. Internal TRUNCATE/COPY borrow a synchronous, tenant/transaction/target-scoped replacement receipt. Pending declarations and selected referenced keys/actions survive internal replacement, including optimized whole-table DELETE. Explicit DROP/CREATE makes the normal new-parent selection. Fatal nested errors seal the transaction even if callbacks catch them, preserve their original error, and reject subsequent SQL before workspace preparation.

DROP DATABASE delegates index-catalog deletion to the existing transactional database bulk owner, removing redundant per-table catalog deletes. Table physical/plugin/history cleanup keeps its existing owner. Historical checkpoint replay retains durable appendable data/tombstone objects; creation registers/prefetches without reclamation when deletion time is absent, and deletion scans stop at the object boundary. Checkpoint DeleteTime and live startTS cutoffs stay distinct. Lock pressure classification uses available memory headroom within existing retry budgets and queues.

### Planning and execution boundaries

- CTAS privilege/CREATE planning uses private source ASTs, including mutable maps and SAMPLE columns. Generated INSERT uses the bound source, and prepared reuse retains exact inferred names. Copies are GC-owned. Fresh statement/PREPARE binding owns deprecation warnings; privilege-only planning and internal compilation retries use the existing internal origin and restore the compiler context. Separate syntactic calls still emit separate warnings.
- Online DATA BRANCH MERGE/PICK performs ordered initialization, production/application and cleanup in its shared transaction. Retry-capable stage/apply SQL cannot overlap an LCA probe. Hash construction and read-only DIFF retain parallelism. No SQL mutex, whole-result spool or independent retry state is introduced.
- Internal physical descendants borrow the root frontier without inheriting its FK payload. Private-generation checks use the existing rollback-aware creation journal. Borrowed CREATE refreshes/rebuilds inside its already admitted domain without rolling back the caller or incrementing its statement. Frontend derived dispatch scopes the existing process ownership marker; common Compile performs pre-effect CREATE refresh and rejects all borrowed execution retries, including prepared reuse. Owning frontend statements capture their workspace boundary after increment, using the effective AST for direct/text/binary execution. A later MERGE error therefore retains prior statements and removes all stage effects; engine statements retain their existing Compile/Reset boundary owner.
- Manual SQL task completion stays with executor/storage. The frontend performs its existing commit-timestamp synchronization once after executor return, before returning success or the original error. It shares the detached completion context and existing RPC/apply-wait bounds; no status polling or new task state is added.
- The embedded-prebuild join cancellation fixture uses the production helper grace instead of an unsupported one-second override. Existing FIFO barriers distinguish drained descendants from completion acknowledgment. Forced-KILL/missing-acknowledgment preservation remains covered by its existing tests.

### Current validation

Rebased onto pinned main `61d8e2887f0ae5b63e3baa7b399e3b10b9c47d6a`. Go 1.27.1, Linux amd64, matching native libraries and repository `mo-cgo-test` wrapper. Existing 67-file reviewed content survived the rebase unchanged; the final intended change map contains 73 files.

- Source service build and complete frontend normal/race pass (69.017s/61.982s). Complete compile normal/race pass; final cached/reset and retry regressions also pass normally and under race. Fresh race coverage includes moerr, databranchutils, lockservice, plan protobuf, lockop, compile, planner, taskservice, txn/client, disttae and logtailreplay.
- Selected real issue regressions pass under race (92.441s), including FK generations, replacement, cancellation, database/branch ownership, rollback and cold checkpoint snapshots. Actual SQL MERGE commit/rollback controls preserve earlier writes; a unique-key failure after staging/application preserves its original error, prior INSERT through COMMIT, unchanged destination and zero stage residue.
- Deterministic negative controls catch borrowed replay on unfixed code and cross-boundary workspace corruption before the frontend amendment. Real Compile.Run tests reject borrowed ordinary/definition/vector retries without rollback, retain ordinary RC retry, and verify the current owner after cached Reset. Common Compile admission tests cover stable/unknown binding, one pre-effect refresh, changed domain, cancellation and CTAS metadata.
- Extended existing branch-edge BVT passes **219/219 twice** on two authenticated CNs with strict comparison (no `nometa`): 0 failed/ignored/abnormal statements, verified cleanup, both services exit 0. The fixture reuses its unique-conflict setup to cover prior INSERT, partial MERGE failure, destination/prior rows, stage cleanup and COMMIT.
- Changed-closure vet, configured incremental golangci-lint and molint pass: 0 new lint issues; 18 emitted molint advisories match expressions on pinned main. Formatting/diff checks pass. Temporary NVMe pressure correctly triggered the existing 16 GiB spill margin; full frontend normal/race were rerun on the spacious system filesystem, preserving that protection.

### Reused earlier evidence

Unchanged warning/task/cancellation inputs retain their prior validation: owning normal/race and optools normal/race, failed negative controls for duplicate CTAS warnings and omitted task fence, two-CN JSON/task data/error/warning BVT **234/234 twice**, and both-direction task-storage reads after **20 failed executions plus one timeout** without polling. Join cancellation passes **20 normal and 20 race repetitions**; its too-short-grace control forces KILL and retained artifacts. Bash syntax and incremental ShellCheck pass. These are recorded earlier runs, not fresh new-head executions.

The earlier strict JSON metadata run had seven JDBC metadata differences (length/prepared label); those comparisons are not claimed passed or attributed to this PR. The latest checked old-head CI independently passed the previous warning/task/cancellation corrections.

### Performance, compatibility and limits

Historical matched 5000-table runs: DROP 66.806s versus baseline 101.825/101.924s (~34.4% lower elapsed), committed catalog 5000→0. CREATE setup 43.233s versus 40.020/40.204s; whole-run peak RSS +0.61% is not DROP-isolated memory. These measurements were not repeated for this CI correction; the database bulk cleanup path is unchanged.

Previously measured CTAS copying adds 2936B/37 allocations and ~4.17% planner elapsed. Ordered online MERGE samples showed ~0%/24%/24% median latency differences for 1/128/2048 rows; workload-wide performance neutrality is not claimed. Current warning/task corrections add no per-row SELECT/DML work; failed manual task execution now pays one existing cluster synchronization. The current ownership amendment adds one bounded boundary update per owning frontend statement and at most one existing CREATE replan before effects; it adds no per-row work, cache, worker or lock held across dispatch. Unreachable metadata writers retain the helper's best-effort semantics. Sustained-contention fairness and uncontended TRUNCATE throughput remain unmeasured.

No mixed-version upgrade protocol is introduced; declarations authored with foreign_key_checks=0 are not newly validated. Cache/topology Cartesian completeness and ARM runtime validation are not claimed.

Latest checked CI at `8c653aaa7bcb42107f6e17b4dff5fc6873fd3bcc` (run 38138857769) passed build, Ubuntu/x86 UT, ARM64 SCA, UT coverage and pessimistic multi-CN BVT. Proxy BVT exposed nested CREATE retry removing earlier MERGE stages. This correction repairs that owner and the separately reproduced frontend workspace boundary defect. Aggregate coverage failed from missing producer output; no coverage verdict was computed. New-head remote CI remains pending after push.

Design amendments use explicitly selected **gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh**, sessions `01a12b76-f0b5-7eb0-b176-bfd8722687ef` and `01a12b90-b7bb-7750-ba0f-36f601c7521c`. Final overall review session `01a12ba5-7082-7ad2-8474-ca93c960d788` reports **APPROVE — no material blocker**, reconciled against all 73 final file hashes and amendment fingerprint `540ba1a5…`.
